title: PR title and description gate in the hygiene job
summary: Adds `osf pr check`, a new subcommand that reads a pull request event payload and the repository's PR template, verifies the title is non-empty, that every `## ` heading the template requires is present, and that each tool-written `<!-- osf:NAME:start/end -->` block pairs up exactly once. It then writes the hand-written title and body to `title.txt` and `body.md` so the existing `osf scan` and `osf lint writing` checks can run over them, and the CI `hygiene` job wires this in, re-running on `edited` events and exempting dependency-update bots.

lanes.subtitle: GitHub Actions
lanes.summary: The hygiene job that runs on pull request events and shells out to the built `osf` binary.

lanes.label: osf CLI
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf
lanes.summary: The command surface: `pr check` plus the existing `scan` and `lint writing` commands it hands off to.

nodes.label: hygiene job
nodes.subtitle: ci.yml
nodes.summary: The existing hygiene job gains a step that runs `osf pr check` on the event payload, then `osf scan` and `osf lint writing` on the files it writes. It now also triggers on `edited` so a description edit re-runs the checks.

nodes.label: Event payload
nodes.subtitle: $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH
nodes.summary: The JSON file GitHub writes for the event. Holds `pull_request.title`, `pull_request.body` and `pull_request.user.login`. Attacker-controlled, so it is read from disk and never interpolated into a command line.

nodes.label: PR template
nodes.subtitle: .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
nodes.summary: The source of truth for required `## ` headings and for the names of tool-written blocks. Both lists are read from it, never copied into code.

nodes.label: Private-name denylist
nodes.subtitle: OSF_DENYLIST
nodes.summary: A repository secret passed to the scan step. Empty on fork pull requests, in which case only the other scan rules run.

nodes.label: pr check
nodes.subtitle: pr_check_cmd
nodes.summary: Reads the event and template, parses the payload, applies author exemptions, calls `pr_check::check`, writes `title.txt` and `body.md`, and maps problems to exit code 1 (or 2 for usage errors).

nodes.label: osf scan
nodes.subtitle: private names, paths, secrets
nodes.summary: The existing scanner, now pointed at the two files `pr check` writes instead of tracked files.

nodes.label: osf lint writing
nodes.subtitle: --context commit / document
nodes.summary: The existing writing lint, run with `--gate` on the title as a commit message and on the body as a document.

nodes.label: check
nodes.subtitle: check(title, body, template)
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the structural checks: empty title, strip tool blocks, then compare required headings against those present. Returns `HandWritten` or every `Problem` found.

nodes.label: strip_generated
nodes.subtitle: cut tool blocks
nodes.summary: Removes each named tool-written block between its start and end markers, replacing it with a newline. Errors when markers do not pair once each or the end comes first.

nodes.label: headings
nodes.subtitle: visible ## lines
nodes.summary: Returns every `## ` heading outside HTML comments and fenced code blocks, so a heading hidden in either does not satisfy the template.

nodes.label: generated_block_names
nodes.subtitle: from template markers
nodes.summary: Scans the template for `<!-- osf:NAME:start` markers and returns the distinct block names, so the block list is derived from the template rather than hard-coded.

nodes.label: marker
nodes.subtitle: find_starts / find_ends
nodes.summary: The existing marker helpers that locate `osf:NAME:start` and `osf:NAME:end` comments in a description.

nodes.label: pr_check tests
nodes.subtitle: unit + end-to-end
nodes.summary: Unit tests for headings, block names, stripping and the check itself, plus end-to-end tests that run the real binary against fixtures and the repository's real template.

nodes.label: pr-description fixtures
nodes.subtitle: good, missing-heading, puffery, …
nodes.summary: Markdown bodies with placeholders for a local path, a puffery sentence and a denylisted name, so no tracked file holds the strings the repository scan would flag.

edges.label: ./target/release/osf pr check
edges.summary: The new step invokes the built binary with the event path and an output directory, exempting dependabot and renovate.

edges.label: on title.txt + body.md
edges.summary: After `pr check` writes the files, the job runs the same scan as for tracked files.

edges.label: --gate
edges.summary: The writing lint runs twice: title as a commit message, body as a document.

edges.label: read JSON
edges.summary: The command reads the payload file from disk and pulls out title, body and author login.

edges.label: headings + block names
edges.summary: The template supplies both the required headings and the tool-block names.
The command delegates the structural checks to the module.
Tool-written blocks are cut out before headings are compared.
Required and present headings are both computed with the same function.
The block names to strip come from the template.
Marker positions are found with the existing helpers.

edges.label: OSF_DENYLIST
edges.summary: The scan consults the denylist secret when it is present.
Unit and end-to-end tests exercise the check against fixtures and the real template.
Fixture bodies are substituted and fed through the real binary.
